entries.name: Crew Roles
entries.text:
Your crew role is an additional feature that can be used alongside your character’s background and class. It essentially gives you the ability to specialize in a field or duty and succeed where others may fail. While it may not provide a wide variety of bonuses and stats, it will be crucial to developing a stable crew and allocating jobs on a functioning ship. Your role should be something you enjoy doing when playing as your character. For example, if you are a cyborg tinkerer, you may take pride in being the crew’s shipwright. This may also tie into your character’s ideals and background.
Deciding your role can depend on your class and background, but can ultimately be anything that would fit your character’s interests. Work with other players to decide what would make for a balanced team, and try to give everyone a unique position and function. Without proper coordination and cohesion, as well as leadership, a ship and its crew could easily fall apart. While your role may not provide any proficiencies, equipment, or languages, it will provide features that will make you a very useful and unique addition to your crew.
Crew roles can be decided at any point early in the campaign or during character introductions. But it should make sense and align with everyone’s character’s strengths and abilities.

sections.name: Allocating or Swapping Roles
sections.text: While a crew role can be decided at any point when designing or playing your character early on, it may prove difficult to suddenly change roles on a whim. While you can officially swap to a different role and perform its basic functions, you cannot have the pirate prestige abilities of a new role until you actively work and study that role for at least [3d6 x 10] days to adjust to it. Until then, can only perform basic tasks for that role and use the regular features.

entries.name: Captain
entries.text:
Your role is very simple: you motivate, guide, and command your ship and crew. It is possible for the captain of a ship to have a number of complex roles, but they should typically be the strongest and most charismatic individual in a crew. Some captains may differ or have unique personalities, but their goal should be to unite their allies in troubling times to tackle any obstacle, in order to accomplish their dreams and goals.
The captain should always have the last say during any group decision or plan. While some crews may not entirely center around their captain, it is important to still give them a high degree of authority over the decision process.

sections.name: Role Skill Proficiency
sections.text: As the captain you have proficiency with Intimidation and Persuasion skills.

sections.name: Feature: Captain’s Charisma
sections.text: A captain is the head of the ship, but should never act like a tyrant when operating a healthy crew. When they lead a charge, your allies should follow. When they call a shot, others should respect it. When they are speaking, the crew should listen. This shouldn’t be a power that is abused, but rather a quality that your comrades revere. If you tell a member of your crew to perform an action, they will feel naturally compelled to complete it. However, if a duty directly goes against their alignment, ideals, personality traits, class, background, or race (or is simply too ridiculous to consider), they are allowed to refrain.

sections.name: Pirate Prestige Ability: Crew Recruitment
sections.text:
*To understand how to run crew recruitment, make sure the DM has read information on “Hirelings” under the Ships and Sailing section in the Dungeons and Devil Fruits Dungeon Master’s Guide.
A character that has the captain role can easily recruit other pirates by spending their pirate prestige points at various locations. A captain can spend a pirate prestige point to recruit a regular hireling or specialist for a week without needing to pay them. The hireling will still need to have their basic needs met, and will demand pay a week after the initial week is over unless another prestige point is spent.
You cannot recruit in locations where your crew has a reputation of 5 or less.

entries.name: First Mate
entries.text:
The First Mate is the captain’s most trusted and skilled crewmate, acting as a right-hand and intermediary between the captain and crew. They are expected to enforce discipline, maintain morale, and ensure that the crew follows the captain’s orders smoothly. A First Mate is a versatile leader, able to step into various roles in a pinch and keep the crew focused and motivated even in the face of adversity. This role is crucial for balancing the authority of the captain with the well- being of the crew, making sure that any concerns, grievances, or issues among the crew are handled before they escalate.
First Mates often possess strong charisma and tactical skills, allowing them to manage and inspire the crew. They should be adept at diplomacy, persuasion, and basic combat tactics to uphold discipline and loyalty on board. Rangers and Bards can excel in the role of First Mate, as can anyone with strong communication and leadership skills.

sections.name: Role Skill Proficiency
sections.text: As the first mate you have proficiency with Intimidation and Persuasion skills.

sections.name: Feature: Commanding Presence
sections.text: As a First Mate, you know how to boost morale and issue effective commands that resonate with the crew. When you spend a minute addressing the crew, you can choose up to a number of creatures equal to your proficiency bonus to gain temporary hit points equal to your level. These temporary hit points last until the end of their next long rest. Additionally as an action, you can rally the crew, giving advantage on a ship related skill check (such as rigging sails, rowing, or loading cannons) for the next hour.

sections.name: Pirate Prestige Ability: Rallying Cry
sections.text: As a First Mate, you can inspire courage and determination in your crew. By spending 1 pirate prestige point, you can shout a rallying cry as an action. This grants all allies within 60 feet advantage on their next attack roll, saving throw, or ability check made within the next minute. Additionally, each affected ally regains a number of hit points equal to your proficiency bonus. This ability cannot be used again until after a short or long rest.

entries.name: Navigator
entries.text:
The role of a navigator involves charting, mapping, and understanding the weather and conditions that they may encounter on their crew’s journey. The navigator is crucial to the ship effectively progressing to the next island or continent throughout the adventure. Without a decent navigator on board, the crew may end up lost for several days or weeks in dangerous waters.
Being a navigator means you must take responsibility for charting the crew’s course, making rolls to stay on course, and avoiding getting lost or stuck in storms and bad weather.

sections.name: Role Skill Proficiency
sections.text: As the navigator you have proficiency with Nature and Survival skills, Cartographer’s tools, and Navigator’s tools.

sections.name: Feature: Charting and Mapping
sections.text:
A player that chooses the navigator role will actively aid in helping the crew along both in and out of character. With the DM’s assistance, you have the ability to physically map out and chart the course of the ship and nearby islands. Sometimes, you will be required to make various Wisdom or Intelligence skill checks to properly map out territories in more treacherous waters. Otherwise, this process should be effortless for your character under ordinary circumstances.
Additionally, you can assist in directing the ship on the right path. If the helmsman or captain is attempting to stay on course in the proper direction, you may assist them in rolling skill checks if you have properly analyzed the weather and map of the surrounding region.

sections.name: Pirate Prestige Ability: Storm Tracking
sections.text:
In places like the grand line, fully understanding the weather and climate conditions is often incredibly difficult. However, that doesn’t mean it’s impossible for a talented navigator. In most situations, if you are about to run into dangerous weather or climates, the DM may warn the navigator in advance if they succeed on their skill checks. This may be done through subtle hints or simply describing what kind of weather is seen up ahead.
In some instances, the weather may appear so dangerous that it would cause a great deal of damage to the ship and crew if sailed through. If the navigator is unable to find a way around this, they may choose to expend 1 pirate prestige point to completely steer clear and avoid the storm or danger. It is possible that the storm may be exceptionally dangerous, so much so that 1 pirate prestige point won’t be enough to satisfy the condition and completely avoid it. In this case, the DM may demand that you spend additional points to navigate around such a situation in the more extreme regions of the world.

entries.name: Doctor
entries.text:
The ship’s doctor is responsible for keeping track of the injuries and overall health of their crewmates and captain. They have a good understanding of medical science and procedures. They can perform surgeries, create medicine, and alleviate sickness or diseases.
Taking on the doctor role leaves you in charge of caring for your allies when they are hurt or in need of medical assistance. Skalds and Priests in particular may excel at completing these tasks.

sections.name: Role Skill Proficiency
sections.text: As the doctor you have proficiency with the Medicine skill, Herbalism kits, Brewer’s supplies, and Alchemist’s supplies.

sections.name: Feature: Advanced Treatment
sections.text: As a doctor, you are capable of understanding and analyzing all forms of medicine and medical treatments. You are proficient in using and administering antidotes, medicine, and other medical tools. When you use a healer’s kit to stabilize a dying creature, that creature also regains 1 hit point. Additionally, when a creature is suffering from disease, blindness, deafness, paralysis, or poison, you can spend ฿400,000 to gather the medical supplies required to treat them and end one of these conditions over the course of 1 hour.

sections.name: Pirate Prestige Ability: First Aid
sections.text: When you take the doctor crew role, you are capable of stitching up wounds and providing first aid to yourself and your allies. You can spend 1 pirate prestige point as an action to restore 1d6 + 4 hit points to an injured creature, plus additional hit points equal to the creature’s maximum number of Hit Dice. The creature can’t regain hit points from this ability again until it finishes a short or long rest.

entries.name: Chef
entries.text:
The chef of the ship provides meals filled with nutrients and warmth to their crew after a long day of sailing and exploring. While this role may not be as extreme as others in every situation, it is just as vital to have. Without a chef, the crew may begin to poorly ration food, suffer from malnutrition, or grow disgusted from eating the same mundane meals.
Chefs will provide their allies with the motivation to keep fighting, so that they can return to the ship at the end of the day and enjoy a delicious meal. Any crew will greatly appreciate their chef on board for the work they put forth in the kitchen, as food is what keeps everyone moving forward. With a good enough chef on a ship, a crew will never go hungry.

sections.name: Role Skill Proficiency
sections.text: As the chef you have proficiency with Sleight of Hand and Survival skills, and Cook’s utensils.

sections.name: Feature: Food Preparation
sections.text: You gain proficiency with cook’s utensils if you don’t already have it. With one hour of work or when you finish a long rest, you can cook a number of treats equal to your proficiency bonus. These special treats last 8 hours after being made. A creature can use a bonus action to eat one of those treats to gain temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus. These treats do not count as a full meal.

sections.name: Pirate Prestige Ability: First-Class Feast
sections.text: When you take the chef role, you gain the ability to focus all of your talent and effort into your dishes. As part of a short rest, you can cook special food by spending 1 pirate prestige point, provided you have ingredients and cook’s utensils on hand. You can prepare enough of this food for a number of creatures equal to 4 + your proficiency bonus. At the end of the short rest, any creature who eats the food and spends one or more Hit Dice to regain hit points regains an extra 1d8 hit points.

entries.name: Shipwright
entries.text: A shipwright is a wonderful role to have on board any crew that desires a powerful ship. A shipwright is in charge of building, upgrading, and repairing the ship over time. With the help of the captain and other crewmates, the shipwright may customize the ship in any way he or she sees fit. Constructing and maintaining a healthy ship will greatly aid in winning battles against other ships or simply surviving deadly storms.

sections.name: Role Skill Proficiency
sections.text: As the shipwright you have proficiency with the Athletics skill, Carpenter’s tools, and Woodcarver’s tools.

sections.name: Feature: Ship Building, Upgrading, and Repairing
sections.text: Shipwrights automatically gain the ability to utilize the ship building rules in the DM section. A shipwright will be proficient in constructing a ship, and can re-roll once on any roll during the ship building process. Additionally, you will only need to pay for the parts of the ship, not the service fee during the building, upgrading, or repairing process.

sections.name: Pirate Prestige Ability: Defensive Coating
sections.text: When you take the Shipwright role, you gain the ability to apply an additional coating to your ship that will give it an extra layer of defense and durability. By spending any number of pirate prestige points over the course of an hour, you give the ship’s hull 10 temporary hit points for every pirate prestige point spent. This coating will last 7 days or until you use this ability again, in which case the old coating will be removed and replaced with the new one.

entries.name: Musician
entries.text: A musician is the moral support and entertainment for a crew that is faced with lowered morale or increased stress. They may often serve as a crew mascot, a charismatic uniting force for their allies, or a means of gathering support from the populace. Although this role may be used primarily by the skald class, any class can take on this role.

sections.name: Role Skill Proficiency
sections.text: As a musician you have proficiency with Performance and Persuasion skills.

sections.name: Feature: Musical Talent
sections.text: A musician can play any musical instrument they are proficient with to its full potential. If you aren’t already proficient with an instrument, you are simply able to sing or use various inanimate objects of your choice to create wonderful music. Using song and dance to inspire your crew comes naturally and should motivate the crew to reach new heights. Upon hearing your music, others will feel energized, uplifted, and united.

sections.name: Pirate Prestige Ability: Song of Legends
sections.text: Performing a captivating song or play that tells of their crew’s strength and legendary deeds, the musician inspires awe and admiration in locals. Using the same rules as the “Gain Reputations” Pirate Prestige ability, the musician may instead spend 1 pirate prestige point to instead raise the crew’s reputation by 1d4 points in a location. This ability can only be used once per location. Additionally, this gives the party a +2 bonus to charisma checks when speaking to locals for up to 1 day after the performance takes place.

entries.name: Lookout
entries.text: A lookout is a member of a crew that is responsible for staying on the crow’s nest or any other lookout point to spot any approaching ships, islands, hazards, or creatures. By using a spyglass to detect any potential dangers in the distance, a lookout will provide a crew with any necessary visual information to prepare accordingly.

sections.name: Role Skill Proficiency
sections.text: As the lookout you have proficiency with Insight and Perception skills.

sections.name: Feature: Bird’s Eye View
sections.text: Lookouts are far better than others are spotting potential danger ahead. When looking from a vantage point on the ship, you are able to detect even the smallest of details through any abnormal conditions. If a location or direction is lightly obscured, such as from patchy fog or rain, you are able to treat it as if it were clear when spotting ships or islands ahead.

sections.name: Pirate Prestige Ability: Sharp-Sighted Scout
sections.text: When you take the lookout role, you are capable of discerning objects at extreme distances. When you make a Wisdom (Perception) check that relies on sight, you may spend 1 pirate prestige point to make the roll with advantage. Additionally, you may spend 1 pirate prestige point to gain a +5 to passive perception for 1 minute.

entries.name: Helmsman
entries.text: The helmsman is a member of a crew tasked with the role of driving and maneuvering the ship. Although the captain or navigator may sometimes take over this role, a helmsman is unmatched when driving through rough conditions or tight spots.

sections.name: Role Skill Proficiency
sections.text: As the helmsman you have proficiency with Perception and Survival skills, and Vehicles (water).

sections.name: Feature: Through Thick and Thin
sections.text: When steering a ship, a helmsman is a natural. Understanding water currents, when to lower or raise sails, and when to anchor is fundamental and also natural to a helmsman. When attempting to steer the ship through any obstacles or rough waters, you may add your proficiency bonus to any skill checks made, on top of any proficiencies already added, to keep the ship out of danger or avoid a specific hazard.

sections.name: Pirate Prestige Ability: At the Helm
sections.text: When you take the helmsman role, you gain an affinity for moving the ship out of harm’s way when under attack. When the ship or those on board are targeted by an attack or effect, you may spend 1 pirate prestige point as a reaction to add a +2 to the ship’s AC and you and your allies’s AC and saving throws while on the ship as it’s moving, until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Record-Keeper
entries.text: The record-keeper is responsible for keeping record of the history, journals, and events while on board the ship. The record-keeper should be fairly knowledgeable and competent when it comes to any information such as when analyzing information, pieces of island history, and artifacts.

sections.name: Role Skill Proficiency
sections.text: As the record-keeper you have expertise with History and Religion skills.

sections.name: Feature: Librarian of the Sea
sections.text:
Although being a record-keeper can involve working on a variety of different tasks and having many different goals and purposes on-board, most record-keepers are proficient in any form of note-keeping and information analysis. At the beginning of each session, the record- keeper may recap the previous session for all players to refresh their memories.
Additionally, the record-keeper can keep note of major quests, story points, and useful information regarding the lore the DM establishes throughout the campaign. The record-keeper may also add their proficiency bonus, on top of any other proficiency bonuses, to intelligence checks when it comes to analyzing any form of writing, artifact, puzzle, or piece of history.

sections.name: Pirate Prestige Ability: Flash of Insight
sections.text: When you take the record-keeper role, you can often tap into your nearly infinite pool of knowledge and mentally archived data. By spending 1 pirate prestige point, you can discover one major clue, detail, or other piece of information about a puzzle, artifact, or form of writing. Your DM might give you a major hint or advantage on a roll to discover something vital.

entries.name: Artillerist
entries.text: The Artillerist is responsible for managing and operating the ship’s cannons, ballistae, and other weapons of mass destruction. They are experts in ammunition, aiming, and timing, with a keen eye for precision and an understanding of how to inflict the maximum amount of damage on enemy vessels. An Artillerist can quickly assess the strengths and weaknesses of an opponent’s ship, allowing them to choose the most effective weaponry and strategy during battle. They also oversee the maintenance of the ship’s artillery, ensuring that every weapon is in prime condition.

sections.name: Role Skill Proficiency
sections.text: As the artillerist you have proficiency with the Perception skill.

sections.name: Feature: Artillery Mastery
sections.text: As an Artillerist, you gain proficiency with heavy weaponry and cannons. When you fire a ship’s cannon or similar weapon, you may add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll. Additionally, you can spend 1 minute assessing an enemy ship’s defenses. During this time, you gain insight into the target’s weak points, granting you advantage on your next attack roll against that ship’s hull, sails, or specific weaponry.

sections.name: Pirate Prestige Ability: Devastating Volley
sections.text: When you take the Artillerist role, you can unleash a powerful barrage of artillery fire. By spending 1 pirate prestige point, you can command the ship’s artillery in a coordinated attack. As an action, all cannons (or other artillery) under your control can be fired simultaneously, each gaining a +2 bonus to the attack roll.

entries.name: Cabin Boy
entries.text: The Cabin Boy is the youngest or least experienced member of the crew, often tasked with a variety of essential but less glamorous jobs around the ship. They handle chores such as cleaning, running errands for senior crew members, carrying supplies, and assisting wherever needed. Despite the low rank, a good Cabin Boy is invaluable to a well-organized ship, learning the ropes while ensuring the day-to-day tasks are handled smoothly. In time, a capable Cabin Boy can rise through the ranks and learn essential skills from every crew member, gaining a wealth of knowledge about ship life.

sections.name: Role Skill Proficiency
sections.text: As the cabin boy you have proficiency with the Acrobatics, Athletics, Perception, and Survival skills.

sections.name: Feature: Jack of All Trades
sections.text: As a Cabin Boy, you’re accustomed to doing a bit of everything on the ship. You can gain advantage on any ability check related to routine ship tasks, such as mopping the deck, climbing rigging, or carrying supplies.

sections.name: Pirate Prestige Ability: Quick Learner
sections.text: In your time as Cabin Boy, you’ve become adept at learning from others on the crew. By spending 1 pirate prestige point, you can temporarily gain the benefit of one feature from another crew role that you’ve observed in action. This effect lasts for 1 hour, allowing you to perform a limited version of that role’s expertise. You cannot mimic Captain, First Mate, or Artillerist features with this ability.
